title: Fetch and Analyze Data from a Public API
description: Use the requests library to fetch data from a public API, convert to Pandas DataFrame, and create visualizations
objective: Students will fetch live data from a free public API using the requests library, parse JSON responses, load into Pandas, and create charts from real-world data

steps.title: Set Up and Test the API
steps.instructions:
Install required libraries:
```
pip install requests pandas matplotlib
```

Create `api_analysis.py`:
```python
import requests

# Test with a simple API
url = "https://restcountries.com/v3.1/region/asia"
response = requests.get(url)

print(f"Status Code: {response.status_code}")
print(f"Content Type: {response.headers['content-type']}")

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print(f"Got {len(data)} countries")
    print(f"First country: {data[0]['name']['common']}")
else:
    print(f"Error: {response.status_code}")
```

Run it — you should see "Got X countries" with real data.

steps.title: Parse API Data into Pandas
steps.instructions:
Extract useful fields from the JSON response:
```python
import pandas as pd

countries = []
for c in data:
    countries.append({
        "name": c["name"]["common"],
        "capital": c.get("capital", ["N/A"])[0] if c.get("capital") else "N/A",
        "population": c.get("population", 0),
        "area": c.get("area", 0),
        "region": c.get("subregion", "Unknown"),
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(countries)
print(df.head(10))
print(f"\nTotal countries: {len(df)}")
print(f"\nColumns: {list(df.columns)}")
```

Notice how we use `.get()` with defaults to handle missing data safely.

Add a density column:
```python
df["density"] = df["population"] / df["area"].replace(0, float("nan"))
df["pop_millions"] = df["population"] / 1_000_000
```

steps.title: Analyze the Data
steps.instructions:
Perform analysis:
```python
# Top 10 by population
print("\n--- Top 10 Most Populated ---")
top10 = df.nlargest(10, "population")
for _, row in top10.iterrows():
    print(f"  {row['name']:<20} {row['pop_millions']:>8.1f}M")

# Smallest countries
print("\n--- 5 Smallest by Area ---")
small = df[df["area"] > 0].nsmallest(5, "area")
for _, row in small.iterrows():
    print(f"  {row['name']:<20} {row['area']:>10,.0f} km²")

# Sub-region stats
print("\n--- Countries per Sub-Region ---")
region_stats = df.groupby("region").agg(
    count=("name", "count"),
    total_pop=("population", "sum"),
).sort_values("total_pop", ascending=False)
print(region_stats.to_string())
```

steps.title: Create Charts and Save
steps.instructions:
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Chart 1: Top 10 countries by population
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
top10_sorted = top10.sort_values("pop_millions")
ax.barh(top10_sorted["name"], top10_sorted["pop_millions"], color="#6366f1")
ax.set_xlabel("Population (Millions)")
ax.set_title("Top 10 Asian Countries by Population")
for i, v in enumerate(top10_sorted["pop_millions"]):
    ax.text(v + 5, i, f"{v:.0f}M", va="center")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("api_chart_population.png", dpi=150)
print("Saved: api_chart_population.png")

# Chart 2: Sub-region pie chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
region_counts = df["region"].value_counts()
ax.pie(region_counts.values, labels=region_counts.index, autopct="%1.0f%%")
ax.set_title("Asian Countries by Sub-Region")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("api_chart_regions.png", dpi=150)
print("Saved: api_chart_regions.png")

print("\nDone! Open the PNG files to see your charts.")
```

Verify:
- Both charts are saved as PNG files
- Population chart shows India and China as largest
- Pie chart shows sub-region breakdown

Try changing the region in the API URL to `europe` or `africa` and re-run.

steps.title: Add Error Handling and a Second API
steps.instructions:
Wrap the API call in error handling:
```python
import sys

def fetch_data(url):
    try:
        response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
        print("Error: No internet connection")
        sys.exit(1)
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
        print("Error: Request timed out")
        sys.exit(1)
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
```

Now try a second API — fetch a random joke and display it:
```python
def fetch_joke():
    data = fetch_data("https://official-joke-api.appspot.com/jokes/programming/random")
    if data:
        joke = data[0]
        print(f"\nJoke: {joke['setup']}")
        print(f"Answer: {joke['punchline']}")
```

Test:
- Run normally — should fetch countries + joke
- Disconnect WiFi and run — should show "No internet connection"
- Try an invalid URL — should show HTTP error
